conviction_note: The evidence is balanced. EXXUA prescriptions kept growing through September, and the bar is low and disputed ($13.5M vs $14.5M) on a name that beat by 39% last quarter. Against that, EXXUA net revenue may not grow sequentially because Q4 was stocked (about 4,600 units shipped against 3,323 TRx), and management itself flagged a weak, low-margin first half. p_up is 47 with abs_move 7: the scale is the name's thin-turnover tail (-10%, -18% and +92% in eight prints) rather than its 1.85% median. The findings sum to -0.1 and the scaled number is -0.42; both say there is no edge.
bar: Disputed, so every size is capped. Earnings Whispers preview (2026-11-11): Q1 FY27 revenue about $14.5M, EPS -$0.10, https://finviz.com/news/421142/aytus-exua-ramp-faces-its-first-real-test-as-seasonal-spending-squeezes-near-term-profits. Benzinga quote page, via a search snippet only (the page returned 403): estimated revenue $13.5M, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AYTU/charts. Midpoint used: about $14.0M. The company gives no revenue guidance; its only guide is directional (lower adjusted EBITDA and cash flow in H1 FY27, gross margin lowest early in FY27, FY27 opex $49-54M). Last quarter's consensus ($11.55M) was 28% below the $16.1M print, so the estimates are thin and stale. My own bottom-up: EXXUA about $3.3-3.9M, ADHD about $9.5-10.5M, Pediatric about $0.7-1.0M, total about $13.7-15.2M.
positioning_check: No options market (baseline), so there is no skew. Short interest is 345,200 shares, 10.1 days to cover (ShortSqueeze, 2026-10-23, https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=AYTU), or 311.6K and 12.9 days at 2026-10-05 (https://equibles.com/stocks/aytu/short-interest). That is about 3% of the 10.87M shares outstanding (DEF 14A record date 2026-10-13), so the short is not crowded as a share of float; the days to cover are high only because turnover is tiny (26,210 shares a day, about $47k). Spot $1.80 is 1.1% above its 52-week low, 37.9% below its high and -8.2% over 20 days, so the guided H1 weakness has been sold already. Market cap about $19.6M against $26.3M cash at June 30 and about $19M of debt plus revolver; there is a 12.6M-share warrant and pre-funded warrant overhang.

findings.finding: EXXUA prescriptions kept growing through Q1 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026): 1,377 TRx in July and 1,408 in August, and an all-time weekly high of 394 in the week ending September 4. That implies about 4,300-4,600 Q1 TRx against 3,323 in Q4 (+30-38% q/q) and likely a record September. The September and full-quarter numbers are not yet public. Management's stated aim is 900 TRx a week (about a $35M annual run rate); the current pace is about 40% of that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q4 FY26 (2026-09-22) TRx rose 138% q/q and revenue beat by 39% ($16.1M vs $11.55M); the stock moved +2.24%. In Q3 FY26 (2026-05-13) EXXUA reached $2.4M in its first meaningful quarter; the stock moved +0.89%. Script growth has bought small moves.
findings.why_not_priced: July, August and the week of September 4 were disclosed on the 2026-09-22 call, so the trend is public. What is not public is September after Labor Day, and whether the rebuilt field force (32 reps in July, about 42 by September) bent the curve. If the market priced a strong ramp, the stock would not sit 1.1% above its 52-week low at about 1x cash.
findings.independence: Same company call as the next finding; read together they are two lines of one disclosure. The Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/421142/aytus-exua-ramp-faces-its-first-real-test-as-seasonal-spending-squeezes-near-term-profits) repeats the 394-TRx weekly record and says monthly volume climbed through August. That is a secondary restatement, not an independent series; no IQVIA data was found.

findings.finding: Q4 FY26 EXXUA net revenue ($3.94M) was flattered by channel stocking: about 4,600 units shipped against 3,323 TRx (10-K/8-K exhibit). Management's own run-rate math (900 TRx a week = about $35M a year) implies about $750 net per TRx. At 4,300-4,600 Q1 TRx with only a modest further inventory build, Q1 EXXUA net revenue comes out at about $3.3-3.9M, flat to down sequentially despite 30%+ script growth. A growing Medicare/Medicaid share of the payer mix adds gross-to-net pressure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EXXUA revenue has never fallen sequentially; Q3 to Q4 went from $2.4M to $3.9M, with a +2.24% reaction. On the 2026-02-03 print (-10.31%) the launch-cost narrative weighed, per Chartmill's headline 'Q2 Revenue Beat Amid EXXUA Launch Costs'. The preview frames this print as the ramp's 'first real test', so this line is where the stock trades.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody publishes the shipment-versus-TRx gap or the per-script revenue translation. Previews (Earnings Whispers) frame the quarter as 'scripts more than doubled, revenue rising', and consensus is not split by product. Had the market priced flat EXXUA revenue, previews would say so. Net of the rest of the company: ADHD (about 65-70% of revenue) has to hold about $10M, with the Cotempla authorized generic in its first quarter. A flat EXXUA line therefore reaches total revenue only if ADHD is also soft, so the total-revenue miss risk is smaller than the EXXUA-line risk.
findings.independence: The shipment and TRx figures come from the same 2026-09-22 release as finding 1. The $35M run rate at 900 TRx a week is from the call (https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/AYTU/earnings-calls snippet; also reported in the Cerbat Gem summary). This is an inference from company numbers, not a reported Q1 figure.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 is the first quarter after Cotempla XR-ODT's generic entry window opened (Teva licensed from July 1, 2026). Aytu launched its own Cotempla authorized generic on July 15, 2026 (10-K subsequent events), and Teva had not launched as of September 22. Management called the Teva delay upside to its base-case Cotempla revenue assumptions. The analogue: on Adzenys, the brand plus its AG kept about 80% of the molecule's prescriptions after the generic.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ADHD portfolio erosion from the Adzenys generic (Sept 2025) coincided with the -17.93% reaction on 2025-09-23 and the -10.31% on 2026-02-03; legacy decline has been the line the stock sold on.
findings.why_not_priced: The Teva delay was stated on the call, but whether an AG-only market held Cotempla net revenue through back-to-school has not been reported anywhere. If the market expected the ADHD line to hold, a name at 1x cash would not sit at its 52-week low. The sign is ambiguous: the AG cannibalises brand price even without Teva.
findings.independence: Cerbat Gem call summary (https://www.thecerbatgem.com/?p=10398062): Teva had not launched as of the call, and management sees upside to base case. No source found confirms a Teva launch since (searches came back empty).

findings.finding: Management pre-announced a weak first half of FY27: lower adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow in H1, gross margin lowest early in FY27, annual PDUFA fees and seasonal ADHD softness, and about $6M of sales and marketing spend deferred from FY26 into FY27 (FY27 opex $49-54M). It still expects positive adjusted EBITDA in H2 FY27. A negative Q1 adjusted EBITDA lands inside that guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q1 FY26 (2025-11-13) adjusted EBITDA swung to -$0.6M on launch spend; the stock moved +1.46%. Guided weakness has not been punished on the print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the stock is -8% over 20 days and near its 52-week low after the warning, and consensus EPS of -$0.10 is below last year's -$0.08. What remains open is whether management reaffirms positive H2 EBITDA. A reaffirmation is a small positive and a slip is a negative; that is the guidance line.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (https://finviz.com/news/421142/aytus-exua-ramp-faces-its-first-real-test-as-seasonal-spending-squeezes-near-term-profits) repeats the same guide. Same underlying call.

findings.finding: Funding: cash was $26.3M at June 30, against a $13.0M Eclipse term loan and $6.1M drawn on the revolver. Market cap is about $19.6M (10.87M shares x $1.80), with 12.6M warrant and pre-funded warrant shares outstanding and a $100M shelf limited by the baby-shelf rule. Guided H1 burn means cash at September 30 is likely about $22-24M. Asked what new money would buy: it would fund the EXXUA field force expansion (>45 territories), which a +30% q/q script trend corroborates. There is no going-concern language, no disclosed covenant breach and no raise announced.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The June 2025 offering at $1.50 is the precedent: the May 2025 print moved +91.85% and the company sold stock shortly after. On the 2026-04-02 warrant amendment (8-K items 1.01/3.03) the stock moved -0.75%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock trades at about 1x cash. Only a raise announced with or right after the print would land in the window, and none is signalled. The financing answer is 'funds a corroborated ramp', which is why this stays small.
findings.independence: DEF 14A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1385818/000143774926033276/aytu20260817_def14a.htm, 2026-10-22): no reverse split and no authorized-share increase sought, only 500k equity-plan and 500k ESPP shares. That cuts against an imminent large raise.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: spot $1.80 sits 1.1% above its 52-week low and -37.9% off its high, with a -8.2% 20-day run-up. Short interest is about 345k shares (about 3% of shares out), equal to 10.1 days to cover on a market that trades about 26k shares ($47k) a day. The guided H1 weakness has been sold; a thin tape with 10 days to cover makes the upside path on in-line news the more fragile one for shorts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reactions on this tape are fat-tailed: median 1.85%, but -10.31%, -17.93% and +91.85% in eight prints.
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not information. It is filed small because the core says file it, and because the run-up and the 52-week-low location are the market's own statement that the H1 warning is in.
findings.independence: Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/aytu/short-interest), 2026-10-05: 311.6K shares, 12.9 days to cover; consistent. The baseline tape (sealed 2026-11-16) gives the 52-week-low proximity.

findings.finding: The revenue bar is low and stale: $13.5M (Benzinga) to $14.5M (Earnings Whispers), below Q4's $16.1M. Last quarter's consensus was $11.55M against a $16.1M print (+39%), so coverage is thin and lags the EXXUA ramp. A bottom-up of about $13.7-15.2M clears the low end; the high end is a coin flip.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 FY26 revenue beat of 39% bought +2.24%; the Q2 FY26 revenue beat (2026-02-03, Chartmill 'Posts Q2 Revenue Beat Amid EXXUA Launch Costs') fell -10.31%. This name has not paid for headline revenue beats.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is public, but two sources disagree by $1M (7%), and the last print showed the estimate set is not tracking the business. Capped small because the bar is unsourced to the company and disputed.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers EPS detail for Q4 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/AYTU) shows the $11.55M vs $16.11M miss-by-estimators. The Benzinga $13.5M figure is snippet-only.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. A near-zero, slightly negative lean fits the -8% run-up and the 52-week-low location: the guided weakness is in the price, and my one company-level negative (EXXUA revenue per script) is offset by a low, disputed bar and a thin tape.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (fact is not reaction): script-momentum finding cut from +0.8 to +0.5 because the 39% revenue beat last quarter bought only +2.24%.
Rule 6 (disputed bar): the low-bar finding was cut from +0.5 to +0.3 because the two estimate sources ($13.5M vs $14.5M) disagree; every size stays capped small.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): the guided H1 EBITDA weakness was cut from -0.3 to -0.1.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the funding finding was cut from -0.5 to -0.3. Any raise would fund a corroborated script ramp, and there is no going-concern flag and no raise signalled.
Rule 5 (positioning does not file large): the 52-week-low and positioning finding was cut from +0.5 to +0.2.
Rule 9 (net of the rest): the EXXUA revenue-per-script negative was cut from -1.2 to -1.0, because ADHD (about two-thirds of revenue) decides the total-revenue read.
Rule 8 (thin coverage moves more): abs_move_pct raised from 6 to 7; p_up left at 47.
